_comment: FITTED within-need consumption distribution: how each pop need's money is split across the goods that need lists. Replaces the vanilla `weight` field, which is not an allocation rule at all -- the game allocates by SUPPLY SHARE (bounded per entry by max/min_supply_share), so weight-splitting gave British grain 17% of the food budget where the real share is ~77%. See FINDINGS F15.
_how: Derived by the balance UI's 'fit pops' button (fitPopDistribution() in ui/builder.html), a projected-gradient solve over the seven 1836 markets in config/presets.json against the measured order book in config/measured_1836.json. Observed pop demand is recovered by subtraction -- buy_orders minus our building demand minus trade out -- which is only legitimate because the building side was verified first (FINDINGS F14). One MARKET-INDEPENDENT distribution by design: a supply-share rule would make the panel's demand depend on its own supply.
_weighting: Fitted with each market normalised by its own total demand ('market' mode), so a large market cannot set the answer for all seven. Unweighted fitting made France and the USA worse while helping the Qing; the weighted fit improves six markets of seven.
_validation: Leave-one-market-out: refitting on six markets and scoring the seventh gives 39.4% mean absolute error against 45.4% for the vanilla weight split, an overfit gap of under 3 points.
_regenerate: Open the balance UI, press 'fit pops', then paste the JSON it prints to the console. Re-run after a game patch changes buy packages, pop needs, or the 1836 start -- and after any change to the BUILDING side, since observed pop demand is measured as a residual against it.

_fit.inputs: pop split measured, urban centres derived with measured PMs, military battalions from history
